Measures
In this BFI data set, the 5 factors refer to the 5 composites included in the Big Five Inventory. Openness, which indicates one’s open-mindedness, creativity, and likelihood to embrace new experiences (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.6). Conscientiousness, which refers to one’s tendency to be reliable, organized, and disciplined (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.72). Extraversion, which refers to one’s social interactions and emotional expression (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.76). Agreeableness, which refers to one’s tendency to cooperate or desire to compete (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.7). and Neuroticism which refers to one’s tendency toward depression, anxiety, or negative feelings (Cronbach’s alpha =0.81).


Data Analysis Strategy
The data for variables O2, C4, E1, E2, and A1 were reverse keyed.

Measures
This dataset includes responses to three questionnaires.
Social interaction anxiety. This questionnaire has 20 items regarding anxiety surrounding social interactions. Items were rated on a five-point scale, and higher scores mean more social interaction anxiety (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.9).
Attachment anxiety. This subscale was shortened by only including the nine items that loaded most strongly on the Anxiety subscale in a factor analysis conducted by Sibley, Fischer & Liu (2005). Items were rated on a seven-point scale, and higher scores mean more worry about rejection and abandonment in close relationships (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.94).
Self-esteem. The Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale has 10 items about overall feelings of self-esteen. Items were rated on a four-point scale, and higher scores mean higher self-esteem (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.85).


Data Analysis Strategy
The data for variables SA5, SA11, SA9, SEst2, SEst5, SEst6, SEst8, and SEst9 were reverse keyed.
